dati_metodo: 135 US unicorns (post-money above $1 billion), contingent-claims valuation model using contract terms from certificates of incorporation, rounds up to about 2017

righe.estrazione: The txt values 135 US unicorns with a contingent-claims model using contract terms from legal filings. Reported post-money valuations average 48% above fair value (median 37%), and overstate value in all cases, from 5% to 188%. The result is for unicorns only; 'about half' is a rounding of 48%.
righe.frase_paper: Gornall and Strebulaev (2020) find that, for 135 US unicorns, reported post-money valuations average 48% above model-based fair value.
righe.frase_slide: Unicorn post-money valuations average 48% above fair value (Gornall & Strebulaev, 2020)
righe.note: Number: tesi says 'about half'; txt says 48%, so the exact figure must be used. Scope limited to unicorns.
righe.citazione: valuations average 48% above fair value, with 14 being more than 100% above.
righe.numero_chiave: 48%: average amount by which reported post-money valuations exceed fair value, 135 US unicorns (median 37%, range 5% to 188%)
righe.limiti_vs_noi: Only 135 US unicorns (valuations above $1 billion) as of their most recent round, valued with a contingent-claims model on terms from charters; our sample is all US startups with a first VC round in 2012-2019 and mostly small post-money valuations.

righe.estrazione: The txt shows post-money valuations overstate fair value in all 135 US unicorns studied, because the post-money formula treats all shares as equal to the latest preferred shares. It does not test this for VC-backed companies in general, so the tesi is wider than the txt.
righe.frase_paper: Gornall and Strebulaev (2020) find that post-money valuations overstate fair value for all 135 US unicorns they study, by 48% on average.
righe.frase_slide: Post-money overstates fair value for 135 US unicorns, 48% on average (Gornall & Strebulaev, 2020)
righe.note: Tesi has no scope; txt covers unicorns only, as of the most recent round.
